title: Eligibility verification against IRS primary data
status_rationale: Specified only in Unbound requirements (UNB-EXT-001, UNB-CHAR-008, UNB-CHAR-010, UNB-CHAR-011); no implementation, test or operating evidence exists.
target_answer: Recipient status is established from first-party ingestion of IRS primary sources (Tax Exempt Organization Search and Pub 78 data, the EO Business Master File, automatic revocation lists, Form 990 series and 990-N data, and determination letters where available), each observation stored with source, posting date, retrieval time and checksum. Public charity status under section 170(b)(1)(A) is distinguished from private foundation status, grants are made to the listed legal name, group-exemption subordinates are flagged for additional verification, and absence from a dataset is never treated by itself as proof of ineligibility.

intended_practice: First-party connectors per UNB-CHAR-010 and UNB-EXT-001, provenance per UNB-CHAR-008, approval and release checks per CNV-GRT-003.

title: Status freshness, reverification cadence and event-triggered reevaluation
status_rationale: Specified only in Unbound requirements (CNV-GRT-003, UNB-CHAR-015, UNB-CHAR-024, UNB-GEX-019); no implementation, test or operating evidence exists.
target_answer: Status is checked at approval and again at release against the latest published IRS data, with each source's posting date recorded and a retrieval target of 24 hours from publication (an operational target, not a legal threshold). Deep reviews expire by default after 180 days (sponsors may tighten) with refresh 30 days before expiry, and any primary-source change, policy change or grant purpose change triggers reevaluation of only the impacted decisions. When a source is unavailable or stale beyond policy, release holds rather than proceeding.

challenge.customer_intent: Sponsors want assurance that grantees are still eligible when paid.
challenge.adverse_outcome: Payment to an organization whose status was revoked after initial vetting.
challenge.conventional_control_effectiveness: Annual or periodic reverification leaves gaps of up to a year between a status change and detection.
challenge.legally_required: No statute sets a reverification interval; sponsors must not make taxable distributions, and IRS guidance allows reliance on IRS data with conditions.
challenge.contractually_required: Some sponsor agreements specify periodic reverification.
challenge.historical_convention: Annual batch reverification of the grantee list.
challenge.automatic_enforcement: Check at approval and at release against the latest data; event-triggered reevaluation on source change.
challenge.continuous_evidence: Each decision carries source posting dates, making freshness provable per payment.
challenge.stronger_alternative: Per-payment verification against latest data plus event-driven invalidation.
challenge.customer_acceptance_likelihood: Unknown; unvalidated. The prior agent judgment is kept in supporting_arguments.
challenge.invalidating_conditions: IRS data itself lags real-world status changes; freshness to the source does not mean truth.
challenge.alternative_risks: False sense of certainty from fresh but lagging data.
supporting_arguments: Narrows exposure window to the IRS publication lag
agent judgment: customer acceptance likelihood 'Likely; this exceeds common practice.'; institutional acceptance rating 'likely' (unvalidated, no cited source).

title: Foreign grantees, equivalency determinations and intermediaries
status_rationale: Specified only in Unbound requirements (CNV-GRT-002, CNV-GRT-007, CNV-GRT-008, UNB-GRANT-041); no implementation, test or operating evidence exists.
target_answer: Direct foreign grants are architecturally supported but disabled in release 1. When enabled, the routine path requires a current EquivalencyDetermination record (practitioner identity and Circular 230 standing, advice date, grantee taxable year, currency under the applicable regulation) or sponsor-exercised expenditure responsibility. Recommendations naming a foreign organization without either are redirected to the sponsor's catalog of domestic intermediaries whose outbound wording may name a program, country or cause but never the foreign organization. Foreign-related grants add OFAC general licence versioning, risk-based anti-corruption diligence, staged payments and use reporting.

title: Adverse media, discretionary holds and explainable risk signals
status_rationale: Specified only in Unbound requirements (CNV-GRT-005, UNB-CHAR-033, UNB-CHAR-022, UNB-CHAR-030); no implementation, test or operating evidence exists.
target_answer: Discretionary holds are permitted only under a board-approved policy listing criteria (adjudicated findings, regulator actions, official pending matters; media allegations only with elevated approval and a shorter maximum). Each hold records reason, evidence, owner and review deadline (maximum 90 days, renewable once on new evidence) and auto-releases, while legally mandatory holds never auto-release. title: Shared charity registry: public facts versus sponsor-private investigations
status_rationale: Specified only in Unbound requirements (CNV-GRT-004, UNB-CHAR-036, UNB-CHAR-037, UNB-CHAR-017); no implementation, test or operating evidence exists.
target_answer: The common charity registry shares only non-sensitive canonical identity facts and holds derived from verified public facts (IRS revocation, Pub 78 removal, OFAC listing, published judgments), each re-verified by the platform from the primary source. Sponsor-private investigation content, suspicions and decisions never propagate to other sponsors; sponsor-originated corrections are re-verified before updating the registry, and release 1 does not offer any cross-sponsor 'enhanced review' flag. Investigation cases are restricted to the sponsor's investigation role. Charities have a correction and right-of-response process.

title: Charity identity resolution, impersonation and data quality
status_rationale: Specified only in Unbound requirements (UNB-CHAR-001, UNB-CHAR-002, UNB-CHAR-004, UNB-CHAR-005); no implementation, test or operating evidence exists.
target_answer: Each organization has an immutable internal identifier independent of EIN, name and address, with legal names, aliases, historic names, EIN changes, mergers and successor relationships modeled explicitly. Duplicate candidates are detected deterministically and probabilistically but merged only with confirmation. Impersonation signals (similar names, mismatched EIN and bank details, suspicious address or bank changes, charity hijacking) open cases. Legacy sponsor records are imported as unverified claims, and charities can submit evidence through a controlled verification workflow.

title: Sponsor-specific eligibility decisions, overrides and reproducibility
status_rationale: Specified only in Unbound requirements (UNB-CHAR-018, UNB-CHAR-019, UNB-CHAR-020, UNB-CHAR-021); no implementation, test or operating evidence exists.
target_answer: Eligibility is a time-bound, evidence-backed decision for a specific sponsor, program, purpose and date, with results Eligible, Ineligible, NeedsReview or InsufficientEvidence plus reasons and rule versions. Factual organization status, sponsor-specific eligibility and payment beneficiary verification are separate. Sponsor overrides are permitted only within lawful policy boundaries with reason, evidence and approver. Historical decisions are reproducible from pinned evidence, and state registration status such as the California Attorney General Registry is shown as a recipient attribute with sponsor-selected hold or warn behavior.
